title: Exam Technique: Scenarios, Matching Questions and the Open Book

header.html: All learning outcomes: method, chooser tables and look-alike terms

All assessment criteria: answer classic and matching questions; use the Additional Information about people; use the open book quickly; manage the time; name the process or practice; tell who decides what; separate look-alike terms
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: The two question types, the marking and the time plan
Choosers: which process or practice, and who decides

html:
1The two question types, the marking and the time plan

The exam is open book, lasts 150 minutes (188 with extra time) and has 70 marks. You need 42 to pass. There is no negative marking, so answer every question. The questions test applying the method (level 3) and analyzing whether an action is effective (level 4).

Feature Classic question Matching question
Marks 1 3, one for each of the three parts
Layout A short situation, one question, four options A to D Three pieces of information, each matched to one of five or six options
Options Choose one Each option can be used once, more than once or not at all

Each part of a matching question is marked on its own, so never leave a part blank.

Step 150 minutes 188 minutes
Read the scenario and the Additional Information once 5 6
First pass: answer everything, flag doubts 120 150
Review flagged questions with the book 20 27
Final check: no blanks 5 5
Exam tip

. In a matching question, options can repeat. If two parts have the same answer, that is allowed.

2A method for scenario questions

Work in the same order every time:

  1. Read the question line first, so you know what is asked.
  2. Read the scenario for the facts: stage, who acts, what changed, tolerances.
  3. For "was this appropriate", decide Yes or No first, then choose the reason that fits the facts.
  4. Cross out options that break a rule, for example the board deciding inside tolerance.
  5. If two options remain, confirm in the book, then move on.

Ask five questions in every scenario:

Question What it settles
1. Where are we? The process, the stage and the practice
2. Who is acting? The role and its authority, including tolerances
3. What changed? An issue, a risk, a forecast breach or a request
4. Which rule applies? A principle, a practice rule or the process purpose
5. Does it fit this project? Size, delivery method, the people and tailoring

The Additional Information about people: at least one question needs it. When a question names a person or group, find them there first. Note their role, experience, attitude and workload. Then choose the action that fits that person, such as a short conversation for a busy executive.

Exam tip

. For "was this appropriate", pick Yes or No first, then the reason that matches the scenario facts.

3Using the open book quickly

Only the Official Book is allowed, and you may annotate it. Use it to confirm, not to learn: about 30 seconds a look-up, then flag and move on.

What to tab Why
Role tables of each practice (Tables 5.1, 6.4, 7.1, 8.2, 9.3, 10.2, 11.3) Areas of focus for each role
Process tables (Chapters 13 to 19: activities, roles, practices applied, inputs and outputs) Who does what in each process
Management product descriptions What each product is for and who receives it
The index A fast route to any term

Write your own page index on the inside cover and highlight the role tables.

4Choosers: which process or practice, and who decides

Clue in the scenario Process
Mandate, appoint executive and project manager, project brief Starting up a project
Board gives authority or ad hoc direction; closure authorized Directing a project
Baseline the PID, approaches and plans before major spend Initiating a project
Authorize and monitor work packages; highlight report Controlling a stage
Accept and deliver a work package; checkpoint report Managing product delivery
End stage report, next stage plan, business case update Managing a stage boundary
Acceptance, handover, end project report, benefits review plan Closing a project
Clue in the scenario Practice
Why, benefits, value Business case
Roles, team structure, suppliers Organization
Plans, tolerances, work packages Plans
Acceptance criteria, reviews, quality register Quality
Threat, opportunity, appetite Risk
Change request, problem, off-specification Issues
Reports, forecasts, exceptions, lessons Progress
Who Decides or is responsible for
Corporate or programme level Project tolerances and mandate; receives lessons
Project board Authorizes initiation, the project, each stage, exception plans, closure; sets stage tolerances
Project manager Day-to-day control; authorizes work packages; corrective action inside tolerance
Team manager Agrees and delivers a work package
Change authority Approves or rejects changes inside its delegated authority
Project assurance Checks independently and advises; does not decide for others

5Look-alike terms

Pair How to tell them apart
Checkpoint report and highlight report Team manager to project manager on a work package; project manager to board on the stage
Exception report and exception plan The report warns the board of a forecast breach; the plan replaces the plan being exceeded
End stage, end project and lessons reports One stage ending; the whole project against its baselines; lessons for others
Project brief and PID The start-up view; the baseline from initiation
Business case and benefits management approach Why the project is justified; how benefits are measured and reviewed
Issue register and issue report The log of all issues; the detail of one issue
Risk register and risk management approach The list of risks and status; how risk will be managed
Product description, project product description, work package description One product; the whole project product; work given to a team manager
Exam tip

. When two terms look alike, ask who sends it, who receives it and what it covers. Level and audience separate almost every pair.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Project Harbor's build stage has a time tolerance of plus or minus two weeks. Sam Okafor forecasts a delay of three weeks but plans to mention it at the next highlight report in four weeks. Was this an appropriate action for the project manager to take, and why?

  • AYes, because the highlight report is the right place to report delays
  • BNo, because a forecast breach of tolerance must be escalated promptly
  • CYes, because the board only needs to hear about results at stage end
  • DNo, because the team manager should decide how to recover the delay
Show the answer

Answer: B. A forecast breach is an exception that goes to the board promptly (manage by exception).

S2Project Harbor receives a request for a small extra reporting screen. The board delegated small changes to Tomas Reyes within a set budget, and this change fits inside it. Who decides whether to approve the change?

  • AMarta Quinn, the executive
  • BSam Okafor, the project manager
  • CTomas Reyes, as change authority
  • DLena Kovac, the senior supplier
Show the answer

Answer: C. The change authority decides changes inside the authority the board delegated (issues practice).

S3Tomas Reyes, the harbor master, prefers brief face-to-face updates and rarely reads long documents. Sam Okafor must keep him informed during the build stage. What should Sam do?

  • AAgree a short regular conversation, backed by brief reports
  • BSend him the full stage plan and every register each week
  • CRely on the executive to pass the information on to him
  • DWait for the end stage report and brief him only then
Show the answer

Answer: A. Communication should fit the person, so Sam adapts the channel and still keeps him informed.

S4Sam wants Wei Chen's team to have a clear statement of the work, the product, the tolerances and the reporting for the next three weeks. Which management product should Sam give Wei?

  • AThe product description of each deliverable
  • BThe project product description for Harbor
  • CThe stage plan covering the build stage
  • DA work package description for the work
Show the answer

Answer: D. The work package description hands work from the project manager to a team manager.

S5Sam hears that the pilot testers may be unavailable in June. Nothing has happened yet, but it could delay the pilot stage. What should Sam do?

  • ARecord it in the risk register, assess it and plan a response
  • BRaise an issue report and wait for the change authority to decide
  • CNote it in the daily log and review it at the stage end
  • DEscalate it at once to the corporate level as an exception
Show the answer

Answer: A. Something that might happen is a risk, so it belongs in the risk register.

S6The board decides to stop Project Harbor early because the port's budget has been cut. Sam Okafor starts managing a stage boundary to plan a final stage. Was this an appropriate action for the project manager to take, and why?

  • AYes, because every board decision about stages uses a stage boundary
  • BYes, because a next stage plan is needed before a project can stop
  • CNo, because an early stop is handled through closing a project
  • DNo, because an early stop first needs an exception plan from the manager
Show the answer

Answer: C. Stopping early is a premature close, handled by closing a project.

6.2 Recall questions

R1How many marks are needed to pass, and out of how many?

Show the answer

42 out of 70.

R2How long is the exam, and how long with extra time?

Show the answer

150 minutes, or 188 minutes with extra time.

R3How is a matching question marked?

Show the answer

Three marks, one for each part, and options can be used once, more than once or not at all.

R4What are the five questions to ask in every scenario?

Show the answer

Where are we, who is acting, what changed, which rule applies and does it fit this project.

R5Which material is allowed in the exam?

Show the answer

The Official Book, which you may annotate, and nothing else.

R6Which two levels of thinking does the exam test?

Show the answer

Applying the method (level 3) and analyzing whether an action is effective (level 4).

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Exam open book, 150 minutes (188 with extra time), 70 marks, pass 42
Question types classic: 1 mark, A to D; matching: 3 marks, options can repeat
Time plan 5 to read, 120 first pass, 20 review, 5 final check
Method question line first, Yes or No first, cross out rule breakers
Five questions where, who, what changed, which rule, does it fit
Open book tab role and process tables; confirm, do not learn
Look-alikes who sends it, who receives it, what it covers
